items.title: Salem–Zygmund spectral-tail and entropy equivalence for Gaussian spectral series on compact manifolds
items.difficulty_reason: Even after allowing the old wide-cluster geometry, the sphere kernel estimates and the named Gaussian comparison/continuity theorems, necessity on positive-dimensional submanifolds does not follow by applying Dudley's sufficiency theorem. The author constructs a spherical reference process with the same increment scale and transfers local curves to stationary geodesic restrictions, then derives a coefficient-uniform logarithmically weighted spectral-tail domination by a two-parameter summation. These linked reductions and the weighted estimate give the convergence/entropy/tail equivalence with constants uniform under finite truncation. This is the independent H2 burden; Gaussian terminology, the named theorems and the quantitative restatement are not additional cores.

problems.title: Uniform spectral-cluster pseudodistance equivalence on compact boundaryless Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least two
problems.difficulty_reason: An on-diagonal Weyl estimate alone loses the quadratic separation factor for points arbitrarily closer than one wavelength. Section6 retains mixed spectral-projector derivatives through the two-point cancellation and combines that small-scale argument with intermediate and separated-point estimates by widening the fixed cluster. The complete Appendix supplies the required differentiated spectral asymptotic from the named analytic foundations, so the source-specific scale control remains an obligation rather than a direct use of a continuity theorem.

within_work_core_boundary.C1: Distinct sphere single-eigenspace/cap claim, not a literal duplicate or a direct specialization of old2100's widened spectral window. The review recommends lower-edgeH2, but the owner applies a stricter threshold after reading668-766: named Jacobi derivative/oscillatory bounds and uniform Jacobi-Bessel convergence already supply the estimates. Remaining732-765 obtains a fixed off-zero gap from the Poisson representation, unique maximum/Riemann-Lebesgue and compact uniform-convergence stability, then joins fixed scales and absorbs finitely many n by compactness. No further nonroutine asymptotic/remainder estimate is established there. Preserve the full proof as a genuine input, but do not independently countH2; this is calibration, not a correctness verdict or a duplicate claim.
within_work_core_boundary.C3: Different functional-analytic invariance conclusion, not a duplicate of2100 or C2. After the named L2 boundedness/disjoint-support composition and explicit functional-calculus principal-symbol estimate, the residual choice1917-1920/1953-1958 is one fixed alpha>sqrt(2gamma);1976-2006 uses a finite partition and integrable O(h);2020-2034 inserts nested chart cutoffs, rescales h and repeats the opposite direction. These are standard applications of the allowed tools rather than an independently advanced construction/estimate. Keep complete authored metric-invariance material without a newH2. It is chart localization on a boundaryless manifold, not a boundary collar.
within_work_core_boundary.OtherResults: Theorem1/nonGaussianextension andProp19/22/23 use the same Gaussian criterion, original chi-radial representation, contraction/Kahane-Khintchine, elementary concavity/Jensen and Marcus-Pisier truncation. Source1636-1642 absorbs a uniformly small chi tail using its fourth moment; AppendixA gives elementary chi moments. No additional advanced core after the Gaussian criterion and declared named tools. Theorem11/Props12-14/AppendixB are the old2100 explicit covered spectral input and are not regraded.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: A footnote in the statement of Theorem 10 says that delta_n implicitly depends on K.
producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: The dependence of delta_n on K belongs to the object; the constant C is asserted independent of n and of the points, but the object itself is K-dependent.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: The window is written E_(Kn-K,Kn] and the sums run over lambda_k in (Kn-K,Kn]; the scale comparison uses min(1, K n delta_g(x,y)).
producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: Half-open on the left, closed on the right; the scale factor is K n, with the same K as in the window.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: The uniform model writes U_{n,k}; the Gaussian model writes g_{n,k}; both are indexed by the finite set of k with lambda_k in the window.
producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: n labels the window and k labels the eigenfunction inside it; both indices occur in the same display.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: The Dudley pseudo-distance is written as a series of squared L^2 norms times delta_n(x,y)^2.
producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: The partial pseudo-distance here is the manifold one of (787-790), not the sphere one of (606-608).

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: Inside Step 2 of Proposition 17 the integrand is written with min(1, n^2 t^2) under the square root, while Upsilon at (1263) is defined with min(1, n t)^2.
producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: Recorded as the literal printed expression; no rewriting or repair performed here.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: The displayed chain opens with a sum over p at least 1 on the line following the same quantity summed over p at least 2.
producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: Recorded as printed; the index convention is left to the author's text.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.literal: The first displayed line of the sphere quantitative paragraph repeats the same left-hand expression on both sides before the square root appears.
The text refers to the four conditions of Theorem 2, whereas Theorem 2 lists three enumerated assertions plus a sphere paragraph.
The chi factor is defined with the condition Kn-K < lambda_k <= Kn in one display and with lambda_k in (Kn-K,Kn] elsewhere.

producer_literal_source_notation_points_.material_note: Open balls, not closed; the entropy integral runs from 0 to infinity.

editorial_notes: Ambient M is boundaryless compact Riemannian, dimension d>=2. M_s has positive dimension, is compact and may have smooth boundary; do not extend the necessity statement to arbitrary sets or zero-dimensional samples.
For general M use the original spectral window (Kn-K,Kn] of sqrt(-Delta_g), K>=K0(M), and square-summable ||f_n||_L2. On S^d use single eigenvalue -n(n+d-1); K is irrelevant there.

Gaussian coefficients and the dim(E_n)^(-1/2) normalization are retained exactly. Almost-sure convergence in C0(M_s), existence of continuous versions and sample boundedness on a geodesic are different statements linked by the authored arguments, not silently identified.

The Salem-Zygmund expression is sum_p [p sqrt(log(p+1))]^-1 (sum_(n>=p)||f_n||_2^2)^(1/2). Preserve endpoints/indexing/log normalization; source subdivisions use reciprocal integer intervals, not a dyadic decomposition.

Theorem3 quantitatively compares E sup, the weighted spectral-tail sum and the entropy integral with constants depending on M,M_s,K, uniform under finite truncation. Preserve the countable-subset definition of E sup and open-ball covering numbers.

Sphere8/9 holds only on caps with theta strictly less than pi/2, uniformly in n>=1 and center. Even n has antipodal collapse; do not replace this by a global sphere metric equivalence or by a widened cluster.

Old2100Theorem10 has one sufficiently wide fixed K and a global manifold comparison; its explicit small/intermediate/separated-scale and AppendixB judgment is reused. Do not add new geometric restrictions or reopen old completeness/difficulty.

For metric invariance distinguish the geometric random-model requirement K sufficiently large from Lemma25's purely Hilbertian tail condition independent of any K>0. Keep smooth cutoffs, nested chart supports, ellipticity, alpha>sqrt(2gamma), and the exact O(h) bounds.

Original nonGaussianTheorem1 requires mutually independent scalar X_n and random vectors, positive inf E|X_n| and bounded sup E|X_n|^2; it is retained as an authored extension, not added to the new Gaussian claim.

The actual core is the necessity transfer1238-1250/1281-1293 and the weighted coefficient-uniform low/tail domination1325-1338, with the entropy dictionary and original complete geometry inputs retained. The source partitions [1/(p+1),1/p], not dyadically. Constants may depend on M,M_s,K but remain uniform in coefficient sequence/finite truncation. Theorems2/3 and Prop16-18 are one unit; old2100 not re-counted, sphere8/9 and metric-invariance5 not extraH2 under the owner's strict residual-burden calibration.
